findings.where: case.value, case.statement ('Not mixed: no archive sense was found that no field source makes available'); notes
findings.finding: The case reading does not survive the defining papers. Two things hold together. (a) The archive extends the field's object: #123 keeps the problem, adds a layer, calls the biographical and structural readings compatible, and keeps the historical Socrates historically real. (b) The orthonymic sense, Socrates as an authorial position the authorship is organised around within a functional-distribution model of authorship, is an ontology the defining papers themselves say the field does not hold, even at its margin. #123 §I.A names Kahn as the closest antecedent and says Kahn 'preserves the biological-individuation model of authorship', the difference 'not merely terminological'. #1576 n. 11 says the nearest scholars 'do not take it: for both, the constructed figure is a character made by authors, not a position the authorship is organised around'. #123's abstract says the biological-individuation model has been 'structurally unable to recognize' the configuration, and #136 (S136-01, kernel) says the discipline's instruments are 'structurally incapable of adjudicating it'. The field's marginal claims are about a different object. F20 (de Vogel) is epistemic: 'The real Socrates we have not' presupposes a real Socrates and offers interpretations of him. F17 is about genre ('a non-historical genre') and keeps Plato as the single author. F24 ('an amalgamation of different philosophers') is still about persons. The composition's own notes concede that what the field holds is 'a neighbouring ontology', and a neighbouring ontology is not the ontology §0.10 asks about. Because #123 does not radically contest the field (it calls itself 'a reclassification model, not a conquest of the field'), the row is not witness throughout. It is the margin case §10.16 names: the archive extends the field and also supplies an ontology the field lacks. A reader of the same defining papers would therefore decide mixed, not equal.
findings.evidence: #123 §I.A: 'Kahn's Socrates is a Platonic literary construction. The heteronymic reading's Socrates is the orthonym whose refusal *organizes* the subsequent Platonic project, even though he wrote no text himself. The difference is not merely terminological: Kahn preserves the biological-individuation model of authorship (one author, one body, one corpus, Plato); the heteronymic reading proposes a functional-distribution model (three positions, three functions, one configurational project).' #1576 n. 11: 'Danzig, *Apologizing for Socrates* (2010), and Nehamas, *The Art of Living* (1998), are one step from this section's position and do not take it: for both, the constructed figure is a character made by authors, not a position the authorship is organised around.' #123 Abstract: 'a symptom of a heteronymic configuration that the modern biological-individuation model of authorship has been structurally unable to recognize.' S136-01: 'the discipline's instruments are biographical-documentary and therefore structurally incapable of adjudicating it'. F20: '"The 'real' Socrates we have not," ... "What we have is a set of interpretations each of which represents a 'theoretically possible' Socrates."' #123 Abstract: 'The paper is offered as a reclassification model, not as a conquest of the field.'
findings.fix: Record case.value = 'mixed (§10.16)'. Replace the case statement's last three sentences with: 'The orthonymic sense, Socrates as the position the authorship is organised around within a functional-distribution model of authorship (#123 §I.A, Abstract; #167 §2.2; #168 §II), is not held in the field: #123 §I.A says Kahn, the closest antecedent, preserves the biological-individuation model; #1576 n. 11 says the nearest scholars do not take the position; #123's abstract and #136 (S136-01) say the field's model and instruments cannot recognize or adjudicate it. De Vogel (F20) holds an epistemic limit on a real Socrates, and Kahn (F17) a literary character in a non-historical genre: a neighbouring ontology, not this one. The archive also extends the field's object (#123 §VI, §VII; #1579 §8). The row is the margin case of §10.16; its form of composition (one ontology with the orthonymic claims ruling their own sense, or the archive's ontology throughout) is for the operator's ruling and is recorded there.' Keep ρ = extends for the problem and record the orthonymic sense as one the field does not make available. Flag §10.16 for ruling before the row freezes.

findings.where: case.loci: #123 §I.A and #1576 n. 11

The #123 §I.A locus quotes only 'best understood as a *radicalization* of Kahn's unitarianism'. It leaves out the same paragraph's 'departs from it in a specific direction' and the sentence saying Kahn 'preserves the biological-individuation model'. The case statement then cites #1576 as placing Danzig and Nehamas 'one step' from the position, as if that supported the field holding it. The full locus says the opposite. findings.evidence: #123 §I.A: 'The argument proposed here extends Kahn's insight but departs from it in a specific direction.' / 'Kahn preserves the biological-individuation model of authorship (one author, one body, one corpus, Plato)'. #1576 n. 11 continues: ': for both, the constructed figure is a character made by authors, not a position the authorship is organised around.'
findings.fix: Replace the #1576 n. 11 locus with the full sentence through 'organised around.'. Add a #123 §I.A locus: 'Kahn's Socrates is a Platonic literary construction. ... The difference is not merely terminological: Kahn preserves the biological-individuation model of authorship (one author, one body, one corpus, Plato); the heteronymic reading proposes a functional-distribution model (three positions, three functions, one configurational project).' Keep the 'radicalization' locus beside it. Delete 'and #1576 places Danzig and Nehamas "one step" from it' from the statement, or restate it as 'and #1576 says the nearest scholars, Danzig and Nehamas, do not take it'.

findings.where: KO 35 ('On the man himself the archive's statements differ'); P.open item 1 ('The archive states it three ways ... contested within the archive')

The ledger status marks those two as contested. #1579 asserts no thesis about persons, and #203 says the orthonym reading is 'not a historical claim about who Socrates really was'. Neither is a contrary statement, and both agree with #123's frame. Composing all four as 'three ways' of stating the man's status makes the archive's disagreement look larger than the loci show. Under C1, this is also exactly where the field's person and the archive's position meet. That should be composed as the relation between the two senses, not as the archive contradicting itself.

S203-01: 'not a historical claim about who Socrates "really was" but a structural reading of how the Socratic position generates the philosophical tradition'. S123-09: 'the historical Socrates remains historically real, but his historical function within the configuration is now understood as the orthonymic gesture'.

summary: The KO is fully covered and the translation table is clean, but the case is misread.
